concurrency.rule: If available Codex concurrency is lower than 32, every assignment is still created and queued. When a task finishes, the next queued task starts immediately.
startOrder: SRC01-SRC04 and every PF lane holding families start together — the conveyor and the builders are not sequential
VF lanes start on the first PF checkpoint, not on a completed assignment
FIX lanes start on the first FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED verdict
an empty PF lane starts the moment a source lane releases a family into it
concurrency.idleRule: A lane is idle only when no executable work exists for its kind. An empty PF lane at dispatch is idle because the source queue is empty for it, and the source lanes are the work that ends that.

assignments.preflightMustReturn: PACKET_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT_READY with every registered applicable check passing
rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.
claimRule: Assert only these 2 exact families before reading or writing family content:
`node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert PF01 'nc_145_8a_youthful-set'`
`node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert PF01 'ar-act346-set'`
A non-zero exit is a full stop for that family: report `BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM` naming the exact refusal, and read none of its artifacts.
Do not release a claim in a worker return. Captain releases it centrally after integrating the bounded return.
assignments.theDiffIsTheReturn: Commit locally. Leave the final diff for the Codex Cloud interface. There is no PUSHED line in a cloud return.
assignments.mission: Build 2 packet families to the builder contract, one at a time, checkpointing as you go. A family that stops does not stop the lane.

rowStopContract.everyFamilyGetsExactlyOneRow: COMPLETED or STOPPED, one row per assigned family, no family missing and none twice. A lane that returns fewer rows than it was assigned families has lost work silently.

rowStopContract.theLaneCompletesNormally: A lane with blocked families still completes. Blocked rows are the finding, not a failure of the lane.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

A non-zero exit is a full stop for that family: report `BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM` naming the exact refusal, and read none of its artifacts.
Do not release a claim in a worker return. Captain releases it centrally after integrating the bounded return.
assignments.theDiffIsTheReturn: Commit locally. Leave the final diff for the Codex Cloud interface. There is no PUSHED line in a cloud return.
assignments.mission: Verify returned packet families independently, in rolling checkpoints, as builders land them. You claim, you measure, you record a verdict. You never edit what you verify.
assignments.seedItemsAreNotTheWholeJob: These are the families already complete and awaiting verification at dispatch. The rest arrive as PF checkpoints land; claim from the ledger.
assignments.launchRule: Launch now. Every seed family below is rendered at e94fcfaa6fcaf31f276158004b9479a2c4e201f4, which your checkout must contain.
mayNotBeRunBy: the worker that built or last repaired any family below
any PF or FIX lane in this dispatch
assignments.independenceIsThreeWay: Not the builder, not the repairer, not a shard that has already formed a view of these packets. A second reading by the same eyes is not an independent one.
assignments.whyOneClaimMechanism: Two verifiers on one family is duplicate work reported as independent proof. The ledger cannot express it, and the assert above is the only way to find out whether this lane holds a family.
assignments.checkpointRule: Take rolling five-to-ten-family checkpoints as soon as they land. Do not wait for a whole builder assignment.
proofObligations: ROUTE IDENTITY: the packet is built for the route the record names
SOURCE IDENTITY: every source binds by exact SHA-256, recomputed from the bytes
COMPONENT SET: every component the route names is rendered and present
KNOWN PREFILLS: every known required fact is written and visible on the page it belongs to
REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING: every declared item is named in participant-instructions.md, checked against the file
ROUTE OPTIONS: every route-determined election is selected
REPEATING ROWS: no row carries written cells beside required cells left blank
PROTECTED FIELDS: no signature, signature date, certificate of mailing, court-only or prosecutor-only field carries ink
ARTIFACTS: canonical and boundary bytes hash to what the record names
PAGE ORDER: the rendered page order matches the packet manifest
CLIPPING AND OVERLAP: no ink outside a measured write box
FILING DESTINATION: the instructions name the court or agency the route names
FEE AND WAIVER: the fee and any waiver route are stated
SERVICE: who must be served, and how
SELF-HELP STOP: the packet states where self-help ends
assignments.verdictRule: Exactly one of PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT, FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED, BLOCKED_SOURCE, BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT, PRODUCT_PATH_PENDING per family. PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT requires all nine counters zero, measured here rather than read from the builder's report.
assignments.independenceRule: You did not build these families and you may not repair them. A defect you find is a verdict and a repair assignment, never an edit.
requiredOutputs: data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/vf12/rows.json — one row per family claimed: itemId, verdict, the fifteen proof obligations as you measured them, and the evidence read
data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/vf12/repair-assignments.json — every FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED, with the decisive defect and the exact failed proof obligations

outputSchema.rule: An unrecognised verdict is refused at integration rather than translated.

stopConditions: LANE STOP — you write into no overlay directory and no build script.
LANE STOP — you claim before you read.
ROW STOP — a family blocked by its source is BLOCKED_SOURCE and one blocked by an open legal input is BLOCKED_LEGAL_INPUT. Neither is a FAIL and neither is a PASS.
returnFormat: PREFLIGHT: PACKET_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT_READY with every registered applicable check passing
DIFF LEFT FOR THE CODEX UI: YES
assignments.grantsNothing: An independent PASS proves a packet is complete. It approves no output and opens no commercial route.

sourceRelationshipRegistry.readItBeforeYouFetchAnything: Look your obligation up by jurisdiction and canonical artifact id. Its sourceState tells you whether there is anything to fetch at all.

statesThatAreNotAFetch.BUNDLE_COMPONENT: 0 — the document is a page inside a public bundle whose address is already recorded. Record the component locator and alias. Acquire the BUNDLE once, never the page.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.EMBEDDED_SECTION: 0 — the document is a section inside another form. There is no separate binary to request from anyone.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.STALE_OR_VARIANT_ID: 0 — the identity is missing its current suffix or its filing-mode variant. Normalize the identity first; the form is public.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.SOURCE_SCOPE_AND_VERSION_AMBIGUITY: 0 — statewide versus local scope is unsettled. Settle the scope before any inquiry.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.FAMILY_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: 1 — several held artifacts match this identity. Which one the route requires is the question; do not pick one.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED: 7 — the corpus already HOLDS matching bytes. The open question is whether the publisher still issues that edition. This is not a missing source and it is not an acquisition.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.STATUTORY_CUSTOM_PLEADING: 0 — a statutory citation. There is no document at the other end; a packet-build lane drafts against the statute.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.LICENSE_PERMISSION_REVIEW: 0 — the form is public and its publisher restricts commercial reuse. Counsel and business decide, not a clerk.

statesThatAreAFetch.MISSING_SOURCE_BINARY: 0 — expected and absent; acquire once an exact address is settled.
statesThatAreAFetch.MISSING_CANONICAL_RELATIONSHIP_METADATA: 10 — no publisher, address or locator is recorded. Settle identity before fetching.

sourceRelationshipRegistry.neverAskAClerkWhenAPublicSourceIsKnown: The previous human queue told a person to contact a clerk 101 times. Zero of the top twenty justified it. If the registry records an official source page, the answer is already known.
sourceRelationshipRegistry.youDoNotDecideReuse: A publisher's commercial-reuse restriction is a counsel and business decision. Record it; do not resolve it and do not ask a clerk about it.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

failedObligations.finding: THE TEXT BLANKS PASS AND THE SELECTIONS FAIL. First the part that passes, so the failure is not overstated: the field map carries 57 refusals dispositioned REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING and I found all 57 of their effectiveLabel strings verbatim in participant-instructions.md, and both of the controlling manifest's obtain_document items - supporting evidence of trafficking, and the certified ALEA criminal record - are disclosed as numbered steps 1 and 2 of 'Do these before you file'. WHAT FAILS: the official CR-65 prints, in the delivered bytes, three elections it marks mandatory, and the packet neither makes them nor tells the participant to. (1) Packet page 6, under the printed heading 'I swear or affirm, under the penalty of perjury:', item '(3) (Select one of the following):' offers '[ ] that I have not previously applied for an expungement in this or any other jurisdiction.' and '[ ] that I have previously filed for an expungement.' In all four delivered fixtures BOTH boxes are blank. I confirmed this at appearance level by rendering delivered page 6 at 130 dpi and reading it. (2) Packet page 5 prints 'Attached to this Petition are: (Petition must include either item 1 or item 2; All Petitions must include item 3.)' over three boxes - certified record of arrest, certified record of disposition, and certified official criminal record from ALEA. All three are blank in all four fixtures, so neither the either-1-or-2 requirement nor the always-required item 3 is elected. NOW THE DISCLOSURE: I grepped both instruction files for 'select one', 'previously applied', 'previously filed', 'pro se', 'granted', 'denied', 'penalty of perjury', 'swear' and 'attach'. The only hit in either file is the closing line of filing-instructions.md, 'Do not sign or date the petition until every required blank and every attachment is complete' - which names no election and no attachment. Neither file names item (3), neither names the attachment boxes, and neither names the 'was [ ] granted [ ] denied' pair or the '[ ] pro se (Not represented by an attorney)' box, all of which are also blank on page 6. THE MECHANISM THAT KEEPS THE COUNTERS GREEN: the field map holds 50 selection-control refusals and 46 of them carry the identical boilerplate reason, 'A genuine participant election not determined by this route. This petition elects one statutory ground only.' That sentence is factually untrue of the page-5 attachment boxes, of the page-6 sworn select-one, of granted/denied and of pro se - none of them is a statutory ground. Worse, all 50 carry an effectiveLabel that is only the raw AcroForm field name ('Participant choice: Check Box2.0 (selection)'), so the record never states what any of these blanks says on the paper, and I confirmed that 0 of the 50 labels appears anywhere in participant-instructions.md. Every one of the 50 is recorded with requiredBeforeFiling false, which drops the mandatory ones out of the required-before-filing set entirely and is why nothing downstream can see them. A participant who follows this guide files a sworn CR-65 whose perjury clause has an unelected item (3) and whose attachment certification is unelected.

All 66 items appear in the file, so a presence test passes. Reading them defeats it. ACIC-PETITION-DRUG-COURT-POST:Sex carries effectiveLabel 'Race', so the instructions print two consecutive rows both named 'Race' for that document, no row named 'Sex', and the sentence 'supply Race from the court, ACIC, program-completion, or case record' against the Sex field. A participant following it writes race into the sex box of a filed petition. Beyond that decisive one, 43 further required items are named by a mis-derived fragment of adjacent printed text rather than the field's caption - among them '1', '2', 'A', 'prays', 'IN TH', '_______ DI', '4.On', '____________________________' and 'A Class _____ [_] felony [_] misdemeanor in violationof A.C.' - which name nothing a participant can act on. 57 of the 66 have an effectiveLabel that differs from the field name.

failedObligations.finding: SEVEN CONTROLS PER FIXTURE, IN BOTH FIXTURES, CARRY A SYNTHESIZED OUTLINE THE OFFICIAL FORM DOES NOT PRINT, AND ON TWO OF THEM THAT OUTLINE IS DRAWN OVER TEXT THE FORM DOES PRINT. This is a different mechanism from the one FIX120 closed, and it is present in the current post-repair bytes. HOW I MEASURED IT: I rendered each delivered page and its pinned source page to 150 dpi greyscale and took a directional pixel diff, then attributed every differing pixel to a widget by testing it against the 90 widget rectangles I read first-hand from the two source binaries. THE TWO INTERPRETER RADIOS, JDF-417 page 1, field Group1.7, /Rect [268.80 356.50 282.48 370.18] and [313.88 356.62 327.56 370.30]. The source prints one thin ring per option occupying pixels x 560-587 and x 654-681, rows 879-906. The delivered file draws a second, heavier ring shifted up and to the right, so the inked box becomes x 560-592 and x 654-686, rows 873-906: 99 and 94 dark pixels added, 102 and 106 removed, at each. Rendered and read at 3x, the printed row 'Do you need an interpreter?  No  Yes, in (language)' comes back with the synthesized ring cutting through the 'N' of 'No' and through the 'Y' of 'Yes', so both answer labels are struck through on the face of the filing. The row immediately below it, 'I want to attend court events: In-person / Virtually', is pixel-identical to the source, which proves this is per-widget and not a global rendering difference. THE FIVE SECTION-3 CHECKBOXES, JDF-417 page 2, fields 3A.0, 3B.0, 3C, 3D.0 and 3E.0, all at /Rect width and height 13.68pt. Each is delivered as TWO concentric squares where the form prints one. On 3A.0 (Prosecuting Attorney) the synthesized square lands up and to the right, taking the inked box from x 263-290 rows 249-276 to x 263-295 rows 243-276, 134 pixels added and 76 removed. On 3B.0 (Sheriff's Department), 3C (Colorado Bureau of Investigation (Required)), 3D.0 (Law Enforcement) and 3E.0 (Other) the synthesized square lands down and to the left, inside the printed one, so the bounding box is unchanged and 70 to 88 pixels are added within it - which is why a bounding-box or four-sided-box control does not see them. I read the crop at 2x and every one of the five shows a doubled box. These are the boxes that name the agencies the sealing order must reach, including the one the form itself marks required. WHY THE FAMILY'S OWN RECORD DOES NOT SHOW IT: reports/actual-writes.json publishes nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes 0 for all four document rows, which is true and not the question - a stroked outline draws no glyph, and this ink is drawn at the census widget's own rect, exactly the case DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE warns must not be read as proof that nothing strayed. FOR THE REPAIR LANE: the prior VF01 FAIL of 20260909b named 13 four-sided boxes on /Ch choosers, and FIX120's control fourSidedWidgetBoxes() went 23 to 0. That control is measuring the right thing for /Ch and the wrong thing for these seven /Btn widgets, whose regenerated appearance is stamped at the widget /Rect at a size and offset that do not coincide with the mark the issuer's own page content already draws.

The registry track names two selfHelpStopConditions: 'The county attorney opposes the application.' and 'A disputed intervening conviction inside the two-year window.' The second reaches the participant: 'Check both against your own court record before you sign... If either is not true of your case, this is the wrong packet, and you should stop and talk to a lawyer.' The first reaches nobody. Neither delivered document has a stop-and-get-help section, and the only sentence touching opposition is filing-instructions.md 'After filing': 'The county attorney has an opportunity to respond.' A self-represented filer is told a response may come and is never told that opposition is where this packet's help ends. Sibling Illinois families in this same cohort carry an explicit '## Stop and get help' section; this one carries none.

The 38 values themselves are correct, complete and inside their boxes on both fixtures. The FAIL is that the delivered records and the delivered guide state, three times over, that the packet wrote nothing on the court's order page while it wrote five things there. production-field-map.json refuses 18 fields on packet page 4 (CC-DC-089 page 3) and gives every one of them the same reason: 'page 3 of this form is the court's order on the request and every field on it belongs to the court'. build-findings.json says 'Page 3 of CC-DC-089 is the court's order on the request. Every field on it is refused as court-owned.' participant-instructions.md tells the participant, under 'What is deliberately left blank': 'Page 3 of CC-DC-089 is the court's order and every line on it belongs to the court.' In the delivered bytes that page carries five writes from the same field map: the DISTRICT COURT OF MARYLAND caption box is TICKED, and Court's City/County, Case No., Petitioner/Plaintiff and Respondent/Defendant are all printed. I read them off the rendered page 4 and counted their ink. The same refusals array contradicts itself in place - its first page-4 entry refuses the CIRCUIT COURT box with the reason 'the packet states the other member of this select-one', which is the tick the blanket sentence says does not exist. This is the participant-facing consequence and it is why it is a FAIL rather than a note: the caption on a proposed order names the court that will sign it and the case it will be signed in, and the packet tells the person filing that nothing on that page is theirs to check. Repair is in the copy and the refusal basis, not in the geometry: the caption is correctly filled and should be described as filled.

Every selection the packet makes is defensible on its face, and half of them are hidden from the person who signs. The packet ticks four controls: (1) item 3's pardon ground, with the pardon date written beside it - disclosed in its own section of the guide, with the warning to check the date against the pardon document; (2) CC-DC-089's 'I request a waiver of the prepaid costs' - disclosed in one sentence; (3) the DISTRICT COURT OF MARYLAND caption box, on the petition and on both CC-DC-089 widgets, on the field map's basis 'the court of conviction held by this fixture is a District Court location'; and (4) item 1's 'I was arrested', on the basis 'the held case fact is an arrest rather than a summons or a citation'. Selections 3 and 4 appear NOWHERE in participant-instructions.md or filing-instructions.md, and the field map's own routeSelectionsMade array lists only selections 1 and 2. Item 1 is the one that matters: the form prints '(Check one of the following boxes) On or about ___, I was [ ] arrested, [ ] served with a summons, [ ] or served with a citation', the packet answers that select-one from an inference (factId null, routeDetermined false), and the petition is affirmed under the penalties of perjury. The word 'arrest' reaches the participant only inside 'check the arrest date ... against your own case record'; nothing tells them the packet chose arrested over summons or citation. Actionable repair: list all four in routeSelectionsMade and disclose selections 3 and 4 to the participant in the same terms the other two already get. Correctly NOT ticked: the other seven grounds of item 3, which the form makes a check-all-that-apply and which the packet carries as genuine participant elections with the form's own words beside each; and items 4 and 5, the transfer and appeal questions that decide the court.

CR-308 is the order the judge signs and the packet says so - participant-instructions.md tells the participant that everything on it except the caption belongs to the judge, and reports/blanks.json refuses each ordering box as 'an ordering box on the order the judge signs'. The delivered bytes stamp a synthesized square at all three of them: the 'State consents, GRANTED without a hearing' box, the 'hearing was held, GRANTED' box and the 'hearing was held, DENIED' box. No text is written and no judge's signature is forged, so nothing on the order is decided - but ink this build added sits on three of the court's own decision controls, on a document the court will sign, and the packet's own record says nothing there is its to touch. The prosecutor's name, both hearing dates, the findings-of-fact box and the judge's signature line all carry no ink, and page 3 of the packet is pixel-identical to its source page. This failure and CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP have one cause and one repair.

NINE SYNTHESIZED CHECK-BOX OUTLINES PER FIXTURE, on both fixtures - the same defect class that failed md_pardon_expungement (56) and co_petition_seal_arrest (7), arriving on a family that already holds a RASTER_PASS. The mechanism is the documented one and I confirmed it in the source: every check box on both Maine forms carries /AS /Off with an /AP /N dictionary that holds an /On entry and NO /Off entry, and /MK << /CA (8) >> with no /BC border colour. Under ISO 32000-1 12.5.5 a conforming viewer paints nothing at such a widget; pdf-lib's default check-box provider invents a stroked square the size of the widget /Rect, and the flatten stamps it onto the page. Proof, from the delivered bytes rather than from any report: 9 stroke-only flattened appearances, 3 on packet page 1 and 6 on page 2, each stream a bare rectangle outline; NONE of the nine matches any /AP /N stream in either pinned source (I ran the same byte comparison that matched all six of Maryland's marks to their source appearances); and pixel differencing every delivered page against its pinned source leaves 445 added pixels per fixture outside every declared write rect, every one of them inside a check-box rect - 135 at the three CR-307 court boxes, 135 at the three CR-308 court boxes, and 67 + 63 + 45 at the three CR-308 ordering boxes. Visually it is the co_petition_seal_arrest shape: the invented ring lands around the box the form already prints, so the participant sees a doubled, heavier outline where Maine prints one. Measured on the 'Superior Court' box, source ink 174 pixels and delivered ink 249 in the same window, with the ink extent growing only 0.6pt in width - which is exactly why a bounding-box test cannot see it and why the brief told me to render. Every other value is inside its box and nothing is clipped; this obligation fails on the added ink alone.

This is the most sensitive route in the sprint and its participant copy carries almost none of the boundary its own record states. The track record lists SEVEN selfHelpStopConditions; not one appears verbatim in participant-instructions.md or filing-instructions.md, and only one appears in substance ('If the State opposes, or the court sets a contested hearing, automated assistance ends and you need a lawyer'). Absent entirely, with their key words absent too - I searched both files case-insensitively for advocate, legal aid, legal-aid, victim services, referral, assess and immigration and every one returns nothing: (1) 'This entire track is a self-help boundary at the assessment stage. An attorney, legal-aid provider or qualified victim-services advocate must assess the case before any packet is prepared, and the referral must be named before the track opens.' (2) 'Any immigration-adjacent case ... sealing does not bind federal authorities' - which the record explains is common on this route because the statute contemplates federal immigration certifications as documentation. (3) 'Any decision about what documentation to present or whether to trigger the sec. 2264(4-A)(B) presumption.' (4) 'Any decision about whether to seek the State's consent so the motion can be granted without a hearing' - while filing-instructions.md affirmatively points the participant at the consent route ('CR-308's first ordering box is the no-hearing route') without saying that choosing it is a lawyer's call. Both scopeRestrictions are absent as well, including 'Do not open this track without a named legal-aid or victim-services referral partner in place.' Also absent: the record's legalDesignLimitations instruction that participant copy must say sealing restricts what agencies may disseminate and what appears on a State Bureau of Identification check - 'State Bureau of Identification' appears nowhere in the guide - and any statement of the durability rule. On that last point the packet hands the participant a proposed order whose page 2 prints 'WARNING: If at any time after the date of this order the Defendant is convicted of a new crime in Maine or in any other jurisdiction, the new conviction extinguishes this order', which I read in the delivered bytes, while the controlling record says 15 M.R.S. sec. 2264(7) as amended by PL 2025, c. 513 exempts sec. 2262-B records from that rule and describes LegalEase's position as 'the packet states the statutory rule, does not repeat the form's warning as advice'. The packet states no rule at all and says nothing about the conflict, so a survivor reads the form's warning as the law.

The four form blanks the family classifies as required-before-filing are all disclosed with their printed labels, and that part is done properly. What is missing is most of the record's own participant-action list. The manifest carries eleven requiredBeforeFiling strings and three obtain_document actions, and the delivered copy carries none of the following, checked by keyword search over both files: 'Obtain Certified copy of the judgment and docket record for each conviction' and the requiredBeforeFiling:true confirm that goes with it, 'Check your answer to "What crime were you convicted of, as it is named on the judgment?" against Certified copy of the judgment and docket record ... and correct the packet if they disagree' - the words certified and docket record appear nowhere; 'Obtain Official documentation of victim status, if the participant already holds any', which sec. 2264(4-A)(B) makes a presumption trigger - the words documentation and presumption appear nowhere; 'Obtain Affidavit or sworn testimony from clergy, a medical professional, victim services staff, or another professional' - the word affidavit appears nowhere; and 'The hearing date, time and courtroom, where a hearing is set' - the word courtroom appears nowhere. The guide does quote CR-307 paragraph 2 and say what signing it asserts, which is the single most important thing on the form and is done well. But a participant on this route is told nothing about the supporting material the statute is built around, and the record's own answer for what documentation to present is that it is a lawyer's decision - which the packet also does not say. Actionable repair: carry the manifest's participant-action list into the guide the way the Colorado and Maryland packets carry theirs.

The record's fee rule for this route ends with an instruction about the packet itself: 'Whether the $125.00 filing fee and the $100 Department of Corrections investigation fee apply is recorded below as an open question, SO THE PACKET MUST NOT STATE A PRICE.' Currency figures survive in BOTH delivered instruction documents, eight times: participant-instructions.md lines 51, 78 and 91 and filing-instructions.md lines 19, 41 and 56 each carry '$125.00' and '$100'. That leaves two assurances the delivered guide makes about itself false on their face. It says 'This packet does not state a price for this petition, and that is deliberate' in the same paragraph that prints $125.00; and, of the Circuit Court Filing Fees schedule, it says 'Its figure is deliberately not repeated here' when that schedule's figure is $125.00 and it is repeated twice within eight lines of that sentence and four times in the document. The builder plainly understood the rule as no currency figure reaching the participant -- it went to the trouble of naming the schedule by prefix and URL rather than by its title, because the title carries the amount -- and then did not apply the same rule to the body. Recorded in fairness: every figure is a verbatim quotation of the controlling record, nothing is invented, the packet asserts no price as due, the figures appear as the subject of a declared open question, and the substantive guidance is right -- ask the clerk before you pay, and the waiver papers NHJB-2311 and NHJB-2328 are named and prepared and delivered. I diffed all 17 delivered pages against the four pinned sources with pdftotext -layout, whitespace-normalised, and the delivered packet differs from its sources by exactly the 28 declared write values and by nothing else -- no source text removed, no caption altered, no unreported string added. THE FAILURE: three of those prefills contradict the route's elected ground on the same document. EXP102 item 3 is written 'participant.date_of_birth = 1991-04-17' and item 10 'matter.offense_date = 2019-08-04', making the petitioner 28 years, 3 months and 18 days old on the date of the offence, on a petition whose ticked item-9 box asserts the crime was committed 'when you were a juvenile'. Item 10 is also written 'matter.charge = Fifth-degree possession of a controlled substance', which is the subject matter of item 9 box 1 (the Sec. 152.18 branch) and not of box 2. The date of birth is written twice -- EXP102 page 2 and EXP106 page 1 -- so the proposed order carries the same refutation. The boundary fixture repeats both dates unchanged and extends the charge to '... aiding and abetting, continued for dismissal'. The controlling registry names this track's only disposition as 'adult_conviction_after_certification' and no delivered fact expresses it. This is invisible to every counter: each value is present, in its box, in its declared field, and the field map is honest about all three.

FAIL. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates them', obtainedFrom 'Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension and Minnesota Court Records Online'; and (2) kind confirm_answer -- 'Check your answer to "What is the court file number?" against [those records], and correct the packet if they disagree.' Neither reaches the participant. I grepped the whole family directory for BCA, 'Bureau of Criminal', MCRO, 'Records Online', 'criminal history' and 'participantAction': the only hits are printed source text inside EXP106's ordering boxes in the census and field map. I also grepped the builder, scripts/build-census-v1-mn_petition_juvenile_as_adult-set.mjs, and it never reads participantActionRequired at all. The second omission is consequential on these exact bytes: the packet PREFILLS matter.case_number '62-CR-20-1234' onto all four forms, twelve times, and the controlling record requires the participant be told to check that number against MCRO and correct it. They are not told.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.

failedObligations.finding: The values themselves are right: all 16 canonical and 14 boundary writes print in full and land on their own measured rules. The FAIL is that the delivered participant guide contradicts itself about one of them and misdescribes what the participant received. participant-instructions.md line 33 says the packet wrote 'your name, date of birth, case number, street address, city, state and ZIP on the proposed order'. Its later section 'What the platform deliberately left blank' then says: 'The State line at section 1 of the order. The rule Colorado draws there is 31 points wide ... and this packet writes your city and your ZIP on either side of it. Write your state on it yourself.' In the delivered canonical bytes that line is NOT blank: reports/actual-writes.json records defendant-state drawn as 'CO' at rect x 393.93 y 380.38 w 27.25, pdftotext reads 'City: Denver State: CO Zip Code: 80202', and I counted 84 added ink pixels inside that rect in the rendered page. The family's own byte proof agrees with the bytes and against the guide: blanks-left-for-the-participant.json nearMissesRefusedByRole records 'This build narrows the threshold through the module's own option, writes the state on the form's own drawn rule'. The bullet reads as a sentence left behind by the very fix build-findings.json describes (rulesOfPage minLength narrowed from 40 to 24 so this 31.25pt rule would be seen). It is unconditional, so one of the two sentences is always wrong: false for canonical, where the state is printed, and true only for the boundary case where 'Colorado' spelled out is refused as unfittable. A participant told to hand-write a state onto a proposed order that already reads 'CO' writes over correct data on the document the judge signs. Repair is in the guide generator, not in the overlay geometry: make both sentences conditional on the recorded refusal for the fixture being described.

The fee half is right and the waiver half is missing, and the obligation is scored as one. FEE - correct: MO.memo.json rules.fees says 'Not fixed by Article XIV and county-variable ... No fee figure is published on this track', and filing-instructions.md publishes no figure: 'The held sources establish no filing fee for this petition and this packet states no amount. Ask the clerk.' That is the right answer for Missouri and this factory's own regression test (scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/test-md-pardon-record-disclosures.mjs) names that sentence as true here. WAIVER - absent: MO.memo.json rules.feeWaiver names a waiver route for this track by form number and authority - 'GN10 under Rule 77.03 and section 514.040 where the participant cannot pay and the filing court accepts the statewide form. Not generated by default on this route, because a large share of Article XIV participants have no filing to pay for.' The packet states that route NOWHERE. Measured by exhaustive case-insensitive search across every participant-facing byte this family delivers - participant-instructions.md, filing-instructions.md and the full pdftotext -layout extraction of canonical.pdf: zero occurrences of 'waiver', 'GN10', '514.040', '77.03', 'cannot pay', 'in forma pauperis' or 'indigen'. The word 'fee' appears twice in the whole delivered set, both in the two-line Fees section of filing-instructions.md. The record's stated reason bears on whether to GENERATE the form, not on whether to TELL the participant the route exists, and it concedes on its own face that some participants on this route do have a filing to pay for - which is exactly the population a waiver serves. A participant who cannot pay is told only to ask the clerk about an amount, and is never told Missouri has a statewide fee-waiver form or the rule that authorises it.

failedObligations.finding: The guide's account of who must be served is false against EXP104's own printed page, which is delivered in this packet as pages 7 and 8. It states: 'The service list is EXP104's fifteen numbered boxes. Three of them are marked (Required) on the form itself and already carry their addresses printed: the MN Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, the Office of the MN Attorney General, and the MN Department of Human Services / Office of Inspector General. The rest are checked and completed only where they relate to your case.' I read every box on the delivered page by x-position and y-band and mapped each printed box number to the marker printed beneath it. SIX boxes are marked (Required), not three: box 1 MN Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, box 2 Office of the MN Attorney General, box 3 MN Dept. of Corrections, box 4 ______ County Attorney's Office, box 5 ______ County Dept. of Corrections (Probation), box 6 ______ County Sheriff's Office. The six boxes marked '(check box & use if related to your case)' are 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. So the third agency the guide names as Required - MN Department of Human Services / Office of Inspector General - is box 9, and box 9 is one of the CONDITIONAL boxes; and the guide's sentence 'The rest are checked and completed only where they relate to your case' tells the participant that boxes 3, 4, 5 and 6 are optional when the form marks all four (Required). Box 4 is the County Attorney's Office, which the guide's own disclosure table elsewhere calls 'the prosecuting authority the committed record requires you to serve'. A participant following this paragraph would treat service on the prosecuting authority, the county probation department and the county sheriff as discretionary.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.
